publication.title: Facsimiles of Egyptian Hieratic Papyri in the British Museum, with Descriptions, Summaries of Contents, etc.
publication.author: E. A. Wallis Budge
publication.repository: Cleveland Public Library, John Griswold White Collection
publication.rights_statement: Public Domain Mark 1.0 in repository metadata; repository requests attribution and disclaims representations about other rights.

verified_facts: Budge labels the work a Calendar of Lucky and Unlucky Days.
The portion containing days 1-17 of Thoth is lost.
The portions containing Pachons, Payni, Epiphi and Mesore are lost.
The two surviving portions contain twenty-three columns.
Budge dates the manuscript to the reign of Ramesses II or an immediate successor.
The day-level signs include good, unlucky and a third category Budge interprets only tentatively.
Budge says the day is apparently divided into three parts but does not resolve whether the scheme represents twelve or twenty-four hours.
Budge says the portion probably containing the Five Epagomenal Days is lost.
Budge's discussion of epagomenal birthdays comes from a separate Leiden papyrus and must not be imported into Sallier IV.
The page includes selected English summaries, not a complete critical translation of the witness.
Budge prints selected entries for Pachons days 5 and 6.
Budge says the opening lines of column XXIV mention two lucky days and one unlucky day but the remaining fragments yield no connected sense.
Budge says all days from Pachons 11 through Mesore 30 are wanting.

lost_ranges_from_budge_1923: I Shemu 11 through IV Shemu 30 (Pachons 11 through Mesore 30)
the portion probably containing the Five Epagomenal Days
